after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the principal $20$th root of unity.
after.worked_solution:
Let $z$ be a $20$th root of unity. This means that 

$$
{z}^{20}=1.
$$

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{20}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/20}={e}^{k\pi \text{i}/10}.\end{aligned}
$$

The principal root corresponds to $k=1,$ and is therefore equal to ${e}^{\pi \text{i}/10}.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Which of the following diagrams shows all the $3$rd roots of unity?
after.worked_solution:
Geometrically, the $3$rd roots of unity have the following properties:

- all of them lie on the unit circle centered in the origin,

- one of the roots is $1,$ corresponding to the point $(1,0)$ on the complex plane,

- the roots form an equilateral triangle (regular $3$-sided polygon).

Therefore, the correct answer is the following:

Find the root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.
after.worked_solution:
The $n$th roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular $n$-gon must lie at the point $(1,0).$

Since there are $9$ points in our diagram, we need to find a $9$th root of unity.

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{9}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/9}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}/9}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the index $k$ of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at $(1,0)$ corresponding to $k=0,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13995561/assets/e797056434dc122218bdc501cd9e1d5af93127658daa14f7c38b3bd7be8b877f.png)

 

So, the required root corresponds to $k=3.$ Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{3}={e}^{2(3)\pi \text{i}/9}={e}^{2\pi \text{i}/3}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The $n$th roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular $n$-gon must lie at the point $(1,0).$

Since there are $8$ points in our diagram, we need to find a $8$th root of unity.

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{8}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/8}={e}^{k\pi \text{i}/4}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the index $k$ of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at $(1,0)$ corresponding to $k=0,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13995561/assets/31a716f5f4abcda0baea7586f732f9009d2cd4821b429d060d985858c61a3b62.png)

 

So, the required root corresponds to $k=3.$ Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{3}={e}^{(3)\pi \text{i}/4}={e}^{3\pi \text{i}/4}\end{aligned}
$$
